controlled_change: One output row and four token accumulators keep fixed Q8/64 arithmetic and BF16 rounding; 32-bit loads apply only to three GDN shapes, attention query/output and the vocabulary projection during four-token decode. The same developer binary is used in both arms; 12GiB, 1,460 slots, weights, prompt and perfect proposals are fixed.
correctness: 19 focused tests and native capture/checkpoint self-tests pass. Three fresh native Metal-validation processes reproduce every vocabulary logit, route, persistent state and rollback/recovery result. Native counts show zero packed priming dispatches, 399 candidate validation dispatches and 532 in each candidate timing run. Capture/operator/verifier audits pass.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: First clear the combined six-case isolated gate of at least 10ms/token projected savings and GPU-ratio upper 95% bound below 1; then exact full-model recovery and two clean alternating pairs with every candidate at least 5 verified tokens/s and lower request latency.
hypothesis: Extending exact packed Q8 word loads to attention and the vocabulary projection can move the four-token perfect-proposal verifier beyond 5 tokens/s within the existing memory budget.
limitations: This is a perfect-proposal verifier with no real draft cost and 100 percent acceptance, not production speculative generation.
Only 16 fixed continuation inputs follow a 72-token prompt per timing process; no 2K/4K/7K or sustained coding qualification.
Two complete alternating pairs are screening evidence, not a confidence-bounded end-to-end estimate.
The capture retains its resource-blocked status; only verified input bytes and numerical identity are reused. All operator and verifier timings are fresh.
The candidate is in a hashed developer build; production source and binary are unchanged.
The 128-slot draft/target combined estimate of 11.6631GiB is not a measured runtime admission.
